df569f4f0b.q: What does Stephen Pressfield identify as the primary force preventing people from making lasting change in The War of Art?
df569f4f0b.a: Stephen Pressfield wrote The War of Art and identified a force he calls Resistance, with a capital R. Pressfield describes Resistance as what hunts you when pursuing any calling, launching entrepreneurial ventures, following any diet or health regimen, pursuing spiritual advancement, or any principled stand in adversity. Resistance shows up at the moment you want to start, every time, and it is intelligent and knows exactly what you are trying to build.

da5e6e20ed.q: What are the eight categories of resistance that hunt people in their journey toward personal transformation?
da5e6e20ed.a: John Wright Sr. originally labeled five categories of resistance, which Josh Kosnick expanded to eight: the Walrus (laziness), the Mermaid (temptations and addictions), the Crab (negative thoughts and naysayers), the Shark (fear), the Library (rereading negative chapters from your past), the Cuttlefish, the Cleaner Fish, and the Sirens. Every person has one primary hunter, though some may have two or more.

e07c29131b.q: How does Josh Kosnick define the Shark predator within the river of resistance concept?
e07c29131b.a: The Shark equals fear and does not attack constantly but instead circles, watches, and waits. Fear does not attack the person in motion; it attacks the person who has stopped. Kosnick tells his clients to move, even if the move is small, because a shark cannot catch you if you are swimming. This applies to actually moving forward in life, even if uncertain in the direction.

58f65261a8.q: What brain effect does Josh Kosnick cite from neuroscience research about pornography consumption?
58f65261a8.a: According to a neuroscience study Kosnick cites, watching pornography and doing cocaine have the same effect on the human brain, lighting up the same neurons under fMRI. He emphasizes this is not good for your brain, not good for your marriage, and will corrupt you more than you know, and he encourages people to seek help rather than find shame over the addiction.

0036c44118.q: What personal transformation did Josh Kosnick accomplish regarding fitness after recognizing his health standards had slipped?
0036c44118.a: Kosnick realized after 11 years of yo-yo patterns with working out and dieting that he wanted to be the dad who could walk his three daughters down the aisle, look good for his wife, and be an example to others. After this epiphany, he committed to the discipline of coming into the gym every day and eating appropriately every day for 10 years, building habitual form until his identity shifted—now he is the person who goes to the gym and eats healthy.
